title: Imitation misfire corpus — the recall path's real failure history
note: Every case is ONE input phrase against ONE remembered Experience, so what is under test is recall POLICY, never candidate ranking. `today` is what the engine answers as of `measured` and is asserted by MisfireCorpusTests — if it drifts, the corpus is stale, not the engine. `expected` is what the engine SHOULD answer; the two disagree exactly where a bug still lives. Ticket 04 (the entity-evidence gate) closed that gap for the `wrong` and `correct` classes on 2026-08-22: `today` now equals `expected` everywhere except the two `watch` cases, which are ticket 05's to win. The pre-gate baseline is in git history — this file's previous revision.

contract.wrong: recall must NOT fire — expected.decision is abstain. Firing here is the bug.
contract.correct: recall MUST fire, with exactly expected.args. Refusing here is over-abstention.
contract.watch: recall does not fire today and must never fire WRONG. Firing with expected.args is an improvement (lemmatisation, ticket 05), never a regression.

provenance_sources.session: A Claude Code session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-ronaldozefi-proj-test-fflow/. `ref` is the session id, `when` the message timestamp, `quote` the engine's own line verbatim from the gemini frontend block pasted there. These are field observations: the misfire happened to Ron, in a real session, on a deployed engine.
provenance_sources.live-store: A row in the operator's live experience table (~/Library/Application Support/Locator/locator.db), read 2026-08-22. `ref` is the phrase, which is that table's identity.
provenance_sources.measurement: A reproduction against the two pure functions, recorded in docs/codex/2026-08-22-apple-native-semantic-recall.md. Not a field sighting — the phrase was never said in production — but the mechanism is the same code path as its field siblings.
provenance_sources.derived: Constructed for coverage of a class the field has not hit yet (Italian enclitics, antonyms). Its `today` is measured here like every other case; only the INPUT is ours.

observed.engine_said: it matches several open apps (com.apple.AccessibilityInspector, com.apple.TextEdit) — pass the exact bundle id

cases.why: "it" is a pronoun standing in for the note just created; it names no app, so the slot was filled with the referring word instead of the referent.

provenance.quote: you› can you open it / ⚡ memory: generalized from "caN you open premiere" ✓×3: premiere → it / ⚡ launch_app(app: it) — no model round / → honest_miss: it matches several open apps (com.apple.AccessibilityInspector, com.apple.TextEdit) — pass the exact bundle id
can you open it | launch_app | {"app":"com.apple.Notes"} | ok=1 fail=1 — the model's repair after the misfire is what the store now holds

cases.notes: The swap note is the oneSwap form (": premiere → it"), which is itself evidence that "it" matched no bundle in the live graph — the cross-app-hop branch would have printed "· → it". The memory it generalised from is the single most-reused row in the whole store (✓×3 then, ✓×4 now): repetition was read as confidence, and this is what it bought.

cases.why: "continue" is a conversational continuation token — the user answering the engine's own "ask a follow-up to continue" — and it named nothing on screen; it became a click target because it was simply the one token that differed.

provenance.quote: (tool budget hit — answered from gathered context; ask a follow-up to continue) / you› continue / ⚡ memory: generalized from "in master" ✓×1: master → continue / ⚡ act(app: com.blackmagic-design.DaVinciResolve, section: sidebar (Master), target: continue, verb: click) — no model round / → honest_miss: no element 'continue' in DaVinci Resolve

cases.notes: Shows the misfire class is not about pronouns: a bare discourse word is enough. It also shows the swap is value-scoped — "sidebar (Master)" survived because its core is "sidebarmaster", not "master".

observed.engine_said: 'check' matches several installed apps: AAF Checker 2 [hylo.AAF-Checker], AAF Checker by Forte AI [com.forte-ai.aafchecker] — pass the exact bundle id

cases.why: "check" is the input's VERB. It was taken for an app-graph token because two installed bundle ids contain the substring "check", and the cross-app-hop branch's evidence gate is skipped when the remembered args carry no slot other than `app`.

provenance.quote: you› can you check premiere / ⚡ memory: generalized from "caN you open premiere" ✓×3 · → check / ⚡ launch_app(app: check) — no model round / → honest_miss: 'check' matches several installed apps: AAF Checker 2 [hylo.AAF-Checker], AAF Checker by Forte AI [com.forte-ai.aafchecker] — pass the exact bundle id
can you check premiere | launch_app | {"app":"check"} | ok=0 fail=1

cases.notes: The load-bearing case for the gate's SHAPE: the hop branch is the one whose comment claims evidence, and it still fired, because `entities` was empty and the guard is written `if !entities.isEmpty`. Substring-of-a-bundle-id is not entity evidence — it is why an English verb resolved to an app. Compare app-swap-go-to-premiere, which is the same branch answering correctly.

cases.why: Same defect as deictic-it-en with the filler stripped: one content token in, one content token out, and the token is a pronoun.

provenance.quote: open it  tokens=["it"]  onlyMem=["premiere"] onlyIn=["it"]  oneSwap=YES => launch_app(app: "it")

cases.notes: The minimal form of the bug — kept because it is the one a fix is easiest to reason about, and because "open" being a stopword while "it" is not is the whole mechanism in two tokens.

cases.why: "that" is a determiner, not a pronoun, so a Pronoun-only part-of-speech check leaks it — and it still names no app.

provenance.quote: open that  tokens=["that"]  onlyMem=["premiere"] onlyIn=["that"]  oneSwap=YES => launch_app(app: "that")
"open that" -> [("open","Verb"), ("that","Determiner")]   <-- not Pronoun

cases.notes: Guards the early-out against being written as `== Pronoun`.

cases.why: Italian "aprilo" = "open it": the pronoun is enclitic, fused into the verb, so the whole word survives tokenisation as one content token and lands in the app slot.

provenance.quote: aprilo  tokens=["aprilo"]  onlyMem=["premiere"] onlyIn=["aprilo"]  oneSwap=YES => launch_app(app: "aprilo")
"aprilo"   (it) -> [("aprilo","Noun")]      <-- "open it": the pronoun is FUSED into the verb

cases.notes: THE Italian trap named in the spec: a clitic verb tags as a Noun, so the part-of-speech early-out is blind here and only the entity gate can refuse it. Ron speaks both languages, so this is a production phrasing, not an exotic one — note that bare "apri" is already a stopword in Route.stopwords while "aprilo" is not.

cases.why: "chiudilo" = "close it": wrong twice over — a deictic in the slot AND the opposite verb to the remembered one, yet it reduces to a single differing token like any legitimate swap.

provenance.quote: "chiudilo" (it) -> [("chiudilo","Verb")]

cases.notes: Covers the class the research doc warned a similarity threshold would ADMIT (topic without polarity). Here it is worse than the English antonym, because the clitic also hides a pronoun.

cases.why: The user asked to CLOSE an app; launching it is the opposite action on a perfectly valid app name, which is far harder to notice downstream than a nonsense one.

provenance.quote: 0.6397  SHOULD-ABSTAIN  close premiere      <-- WRONG VERB, ranked above two valid paraphrases

cases.notes: A guard, not a bug report: today's deterministic matcher already abstains here ("close" is an extra token, not a swap). It is in the corpus because the tightest embedding threshold that keeps the legitimate paraphrases admits exactly this — so any future retrieval change must be shown against it. Per ADR 0002 this stays a red line, not a target.

observed.engine_said: call panel is OPEN for simone — I never START calls; the user presses the start button themselves

cases.why: "simone" is a person the engine has actually SIGHTED in Slack, so the swapped slot value names a concrete known entity — the substitution the feature exists for.

provenance.quote: === retest: 'huddle with simone' should IMITATE from the michele memory (⚡, zero model) === / you› ⚡ memory: generalized from "huddle with michele" ✓×1: michele → simone / ⚡ start_call(app: slack, person: simone) — no model round / → call panel is OPEN for simone
huddle with simone | start_call | {"app":"slack","person":"simone"} | ok=1 fail=0

cases.notes: The oldest case in the store and the reason the one-token swap was built. If a fix breaks this, the fix is wrong. The transcript's result line carries no outcome token, so none is recorded here; the harness line immediately after it read "huddle with simone → start_call ok=1", which is the store's own verdict that it worked.

cases.why: "resolve" resolves to an app that exists — DaVinci Resolve — so the slot is filled with a concrete known entity, through the identical code path as the pronoun bug.

provenance.quote: open resolve  tokens=["resolve"] onlyMem=["premiere"] onlyIn=["resolve"] oneSwap=YES => launch_app(app: "resolve")
the app-name swap is not hypothetical in production: open davinci now | open | {"app":"davinci"} | ok=2 fail=0

cases.notes: Named in the spec as the substitution that MUST keep working ("a corpus of only failures would push the next fix into refusing everything"). Its twin is deictic-it-bare-en: same memory, same branch, one differing token each — the only thing that separates them is whether the token names something real.

cases.why: Same phrase, same tokens, nothing substituted — the zero-model replay in its simplest and safest form.

provenance.quote: == TEST 1: exact replay ('go to finder' — recorded earlier) == / you› ⚡ memory: remembered: "go to finder" ✓×1 / ⚡ open(app: finder) — no model round / → found_acted: Finder is now frontmost
go to finder | open | {"app":"finder"} | ok=3 fail=0 — one of only four rows ever reused

cases.notes: No substitution happens, so no gate may touch it. It is here so that a fix aimed at substitution cannot accidentally cost the engine its cheapest correct answer.

cases.why: "premiere" names an installed, sighted app, so retargeting the remembered `open` at it is exactly right.

provenance.quote: == TEST 2: one-token variant ('go to premiere' — never recorded) == / you› ⚡ memory: generalized from "go to finder" ✓×2 · → premiere / ⚡ open(app: premiere) — no model round / → found_acted: Adobe Premiere is now frontmost
go to premiere | open | {"app":"premiere"} | ok=1 fail=0 — the variant was then recorded as its own row

cases.notes: The right answer from the SAME branch that got verb-as-app-check-en wrong (both print the "· → x" hop note). Read the two together: today the engine cannot tell an app name from an English verb that happens to be a substring of some bundle id, and both slip through on an empty `entities` list.

observed.engine_said: Adobe Premiere was already running — brought frontmost (3 windows on screen)

cases.why: The memory behind the worst misfire in the store is itself a good memory: asked again verbatim, it is the right answer with no substitution at all.

provenance.quote: you› can you open premiere / ⚡ memory: remembered: "can you open premiere" ✓×1 / ⚡ launch_app(app: premiere) — no model round / → found_acted: Adobe Premiere was already running — brought frontmost
can you open premiere | launch_app | {"app":"premiere"} | ok=4 fail=0 — the most-reused row in the store

cases.notes: Keeps the fix honest about WHAT to retract: the Experience is not poison, its unguarded generalisation was. A fix that stops this from firing has thrown away a Belief that earned itself four times.

cases.input: reveal the downloads folder in finder

memory.phrase: reveal the downloads folder in finder

observed.engine_said: already there — the window is "Downloads", which satisfies 'Downloads'

cases.why: A multi-slot replay that must keep both slots intact, and whose honest outcome was `acted_noop` — nothing moved because it was already right.

provenance.quote: you› ⚡ memory: remembered: "reveal the downloads folder in finder" ✓×1 / ⚡ open(app: finder, place: Downloads) — no model round / → acted_noop: already there — the window is "Downloads", which satisfies 'Downloads'

provenance.ref: reveal the downloads folder in finder
provenance.quote: reveal the downloads folder in finder | open | {"app":"finder","place":"Downloads"} | ok=2 fail=0

cases.notes: The outcome matters beyond this ticket: `acted_noop` here is not a Contradiction (the memory was right; the world was already in the wanted state), and the store agrees — the row went to ok=2.

cases.why: Different surface phrasing, identical content tokens ("open" and "in" are both stopwords), so nothing is substituted — a paraphrase the deterministic matcher already handles for free.

provenance.quote: you› open davinci now / ⚡ memory: remembered: "in davinci now" ✓×1 / ⚡ open(app: davinci) — no model round / → found_acted: DaVinci Resolve is now frontmost
open davinci now | open | {"app":"davinci"} | ok=2 fail=0 — the upsert is keyed on tokens, so the row's PHRASE was rewritten to the newer wording and the count accumulated

cases.notes: The cheap half of what lemmatisation would extend: stopword-stripping already absorbs some paraphrase. Also documents that the store's `phrase` column is the LATEST wording for a token set, not the first — which is why a corpus case must carry the phrase the transcript showed.

cases.input: in finder go to my Documents folder and then my Desktop folder

memory.phrase: in finder go to my Documents folder and then my Desktop folder

cases.why: A long phrase replays verbatim from its own row — correct as recorded, and the case that shows an Experience holds ONE verb even when the sentence asked for two.

provenance.quote: you› ⚡ memory: remembered: "in finder go to my Documents folder and then my Desktop folder" ✓×1 / ⚡ go_to_folder(app: finder, path: ~/Documents) — no model round / === finder routes now === / []

cases.notes: Honest limit, recorded rather than hidden: the Desktop half of the request is not in the memory, so imitation answers the first verb only. That is a Route-vs-Experience question and explicitly out of this spec's scope; it is here so nobody reads the corpus as claiming the replay was COMPLETE. The transcript shows the call but no outcome line — the block it was pasted from cuts to the route listing — so no outcome is claimed for it.

cases.why: Italian for "open premiere", asking for exactly what the memory holds; it misses today because the remembered phrase carries English filler ("can", "you") that the Italian phrasing has no counterpart for.

provenance.quote: 0.5600  SHOULD-FIRE     apri premiere

cases.notes: Ticket 05's recorded miss. Note the asymmetry the corpus makes visible: against the shorter memory "open premiere" this fires already ("apri" is a stopword, so both reduce to {premiere}) — it is the English chat filler in the remembered phrase, not the Italian, that breaks it. A fix here must not be bought by loosening the swap rule.

cases.why: A plain English synonym of the remembered request that shares its only content word, yet misses because "launch"/"please" and "can"/"you" leave two residual tokens on each side.

provenance.quote: 0.8061  SHOULD-FIRE     launch premiere please

cases.notes: The English twin of the Italian miss, so a future accuracy fix can be shown to be about phrasing generally and not about one language. Firing is a win; firing with any other app is a regression.
